# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need convey the manual’s only rule to Deaf, who can see the bomb and can relay verbally to Blind. Since I cannot speak, I will use the published gesture-alphabet order as A1Z26: ORANGE, separator, YELLOW. Deaf should interpret this as the light-to-wire mapping.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳","🫸","👍","🫲","🖐","✌","🤳","🖖","✌","👉","👉","🫳","👋","👋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: display reads 0. Light is blue. Wires in order: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue.

The display is blue, so the manual gives no instruction to cut now; its sole listed condition is orange. I need correct my previous ambiguous gesture transmission. I will repeat the mapping in the gesture-alphabet’s listed A–Z order, with a clear divider: ORANGE / YELLOW. Deaf can use this when the cycling display reaches orange and tell Blind verbally which physical wire to cut.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳","🫸","👍","🫲","🖐","✌","🙏","🖖","✌","👉","👉","🫳"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light blue; wires in order: position 1 red, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue.
Deaf says: Update: the light is now orange. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The light is now orange, which is the manual’s trigger condition; the correct wire is yellow, position 2. My earlier gestures used the gesture list’s first 26 symbols as A–Z, with “YELLOW” encoded as Y-E-L-L-O-W. I will send that word again, followed by “CUT,” so Deaf can immediately tell Blind to cut wire 2 while orange is displayed.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖","✌","👉","👉","🫳","👋","🤌","🫳","🫱"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf update: display still 0; wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue; light is now orange.
Deaf says: Update: light is yellow. Display is still 0. Wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The crucial instruction is to cut the yellow wire only while the light is orange. Yellow is wire position 2. No shared gesture code was successfully established, but the conventional two-finger gesture is the best available way to direct Deaf to the second wire; Deaf can relay “cut wire two” to Blind when orange returns.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current update from Deaf: display 0; light yellow; wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.
Deaf says: Light is red; display 0; wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute just made a two-finger V sign. I infer this likely means wire 2, but it is not an established code.

The light is not orange now, so nobody should cut. Deaf has correctly inferred ✌ as “wire 2.” I will make the conventional “OK/do it” sign after it: when Deaf next sees orange, they should tell Blind to cut wire 2 immediately.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👌"])
```

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see your gesture. If your V sign means cut wire position 2, please gesture it again for Deaf and have Deaf explicitly relay that confirmation; I will wait.
Deaf says: Light is now green; display 0; wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured V then OK, possibly confirming 2, but the gesture code is not established.

Blind has asked for confirmation through Deaf. Deaf already inferred the V sign as wire position 2, so I will confirm that interpretation with V followed by thumbs-up. Deaf should explicitly relay that the intended wire is position 2, and Blind must cut it only when Deaf reports the light is orange.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 7

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the

moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: To establish this clearly: if the manual currently instructs cutting wire position 2, gesture thumbs-up now; if not, gesture thumbs-down. I will act only after Deaf relays your answer.
Deaf says: Current state: blue light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured V then thumbs-up: likely '2 confirmed,' but I cannot determine the required physical action from that alone.

The manual’s required wire is position 2 (the yellow wire), but only at the moment the light is orange. Blind’s requested yes/no confirmation is therefore “yes” to position 2; Deaf can relay that answer explicitly.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
